pr_title: Don't emit octal escape for null character followed by digit
pr_comments:
Is this correct?

I think `\09` should be printed as `\09`, not `\x009`

Yes.

In Rust, `"\07"` means `<null character><the digit "7">`, but in JS it means `<the character with codepoint 0o07>`. So it's not sufficient to just replace the null character with `\0` when writing a string, because it might be followed by a number, and then JS will treat it as an octal escape.

Currently, SWC changes string literals: if you input `"\x007"` (which means `<null character><the digit "7">` in JS), it outputs `"\07"`, which is different. Try running `"\x007" === "\07"` in your browser console.

As for `"\09"` specifically, it _ought_ to be equivalent to `<null character><the digit "9">` in JS, because `9` is not an octal digit. This is the case in sloppy mode, but in strict mode it's a syntax error (see #361). So to be safe for 8/9 it's best to always output a full hex-escaped null character (`\x00`) whenever a null character is followed by a number.
And I just remembered, [I fixed the same bug in Uglify a few years ago](https://github.com/mishoo/UglifyJS2/pull/2273), if you want to see more discussion

issue_context.title: Invalid octal escape emitted for null character followed by number
issue_context.body:
```sh
> npx swc --version
@swc/cli: 0.1.18
@swc/core: 1.0.39
```

Input:
```js
'use strict';
'\x001'; // === '\0' + '1'
'\x009'; // === '\0' + '9'
```

Expected output:
```js
'use strict';
'\x001';
'\x009';
```

Actual output:
```js
'use strict';
'\01'; // === '\x01' in sloppy mode
'\09'; // === '\x009' in sloppy mode
```

Both strings are syntax errors in strict mode, even though `9` is not a valid octal digit.

The spec is weird about octal escape sequences in strict mode (see [section 7.8.4 of ES5](https://www.ecma-international.org/ecma-262/5.1/index.html#sec-7.8.4)).
The `EscapeSequence` production (without sloppy mode extensions) is defined as:
```
EscapeSequence = CharacterEscapeSequence
               | 0 [lookahead ∉ DecimalDigit]
               | HexEscapeSequence
               | UnicodeEscapeSequence
```
...which forbids null-character escapes if `\0` is followed by any `DecimalDigit`, not any `OctalDigit` like one might expect. So even though `'\09'` in sloppy mode is a valid string (equal to `'\0' + '9'`) which does not contain an octal escape, in strict mode it is a syntax error due to containing an octal escape!
